q-65090.name: Question 1
q-65090.worked_solution:
The period of $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ is $2\pi .$ Therefore, for integer $n$ we have

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+2n\pi ).
$$

Substituting $n=-10$ into the right-hand-side gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-20\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if $\operatorname{sin}⁡x=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3},$ then $\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-20\pi )=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}.$

Finally, then

$$
\sqrt{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(x-20\pi )=\sqrt{5}(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3})=\frac{5}{3}.
$$

Question 1

If sin⁡x=53, then 5sin⁡(x−20π)=

a
53
b
205π
c
−53
d
20π−53
e
53−20π
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The period of y=sin⁡x is 2π. Therefore, for integer n we have

sin⁡x=sin⁡(x+2nπ).

Substituting n=−10 into the right-hand-side gives

sin⁡x=sin⁡(x−20π).

Therefore, if sin⁡x=53, then sin⁡(x−20π)=53.

Finally, then 5sin⁡(x−20π)=5(53)=53.

q-103206.name: Question 2
q-103206.worked_solution:
The period of $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ is $2\pi .$ Therefore, for any integer $n$ we have

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+2n\pi ).
$$

Substituting $n=5$ into the right-hand-side gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡x=\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+10\pi ).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, if $\operatorname{sin}⁡x=-\frac{5}{6},$ then $\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+10\pi )=-\frac{5}{6}.$

Finally, then

$$
\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{sin}⁡(x+10\pi )+2 & =-(-\frac{5}{6})+2 \\  & =\frac{5}{6}+2 \\  & =\frac{17}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

If sin⁡x=−56, then −sin⁡(x+10π)+2=

a
176
b
10π−56
c
−56−6π
d
76
e
56+10π
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The period of y=sin⁡x is 2π. Therefore, for any integer n we have sin⁡x=sin⁡(x+2nπ).

Substituting n=5 into the right-hand-side gives sin⁡x=sin⁡(x+10π).

Therefore, if sin⁡x=−56, then sin⁡(x+10π)=−56.

Finally, then −sin⁡(x+10π)+2=−(−56)+2=56+2=176.

q-136616.name: Question 3
q-136616.worked_solution:
First, let's recall the graph of $y=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14269832/assets/08d442eff9febe44bd39e6c15c998d76d56d17bbb7a676d2d511771479bb2f29.png)

Our graph has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin. If we rotate the graph ${180}^{∘}$ around the origin, we get the same picture. This means that $\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ is an *odd* function, and we have

$$
\operatorname{sin}⁡(-x)=-\operatorname{sin}⁡x.
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡(-a) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡a \\  & =-0.72.\end{aligned}
$$
